Take the blocks off a server as text, and read them back

Source: R/blocks_server.R
export_blocks.Rd

export_blocks() prints the raw value of each block as R code, in pages with a checksum. import_blocks() reads the captured pages into <version>_results/real/blocks.qs2, and read_blocks() returns those values for a manuscript.

Usage

export_blocks(version = NULL)

import_blocks(version, home = ".")

read_blocks(version, home = ".")

Arguments

version

The version, for example "v01". For export_blocks(), the default NULL is the version of the last initialize_project() in this R session.

home

The project folder. The default "." is the working folder.

Value

export_blocks(): invisibly, the printed lines. import_blocks(): invisibly, the path of the blocks.qs2 that it wrote. read_blocks(): a named list with the raw value of each block.

Details

export_blocks()

export_blocks() runs on the server, after the file of to_one_file(). It needs initialize_project() in this R session, and it reads the blocks and the real results as show_blocks() does. For each block, it keeps the raw value, the value that save_results() writes to blocks.qs2. It does not call the formatter of a block(). It turns a data.table into a data.frame, because R cannot read the pointer of a data.table back. It stops on a block that stops, and the error names the block.

The text of block k is the output of base R dput() for a list. The list holds one element: the raw value, with the name of the block. The control of dput() is c("keepNA", "keepInteger", "niceNames", "showAttributes", "digits17"). With "digits17", each number has 17 significant digits, so the number after the import is the same double.

Each page has at most 35 lines: a header line and at most 34 lines of text. The header line is pbn-blocks <version> run <run date> block <k>/<n> page <p>/<P> md5 <m>. The run date is that of show_block(). <m> is the first 8 hex characters of tools::md5sum() of the text lines of the page. pbn takes them without trailing white space, joined by "\n", with no final newline. An empty line follows each page.

When the real results have fake_real_data TRUE in their manifest, each header line ends with the token fake. Examples are a run of a one-file project on this computer, see initialize_project(). The pages of real data have no token.

import_blocks()

Copy or type the pages from the screen of the server into <version>_results/real/export_blocks.txt. import_blocks() reads that file. It removes the trailing white space of each line and each empty line, and it ignores the lines before the first header line. The lines after a header line, up to the next header line, are the text of that page.

import_blocks() stops and writes nothing when:

  • the file has no header line,

  • a header line names another version, or the pages name more than one run date or more than one count of blocks,

  • some header lines end with the token fake and some do not,

  • the md5 of the text of a page differs from its header, and the error names the block and the page,

  • a page is missing, and the error names the block and the page,

  • a page comes twice with other text. A page that comes twice with the same text counts once.

  • R cannot parse the text of a block, or the text is not a list of one named value.

It rebuilds each value with eval(parse(text = text), envir = baseenv()). So import only the pages that export_blocks() printed, because import_blocks() runs the file as R code. It writes the named list of the values to <version>_results/real/blocks.qs2 and overwrites that file. It writes there in a one-file project too, where the scenario real of this computer is in fake/, see initialize_project(). When the pages end with the token fake, the list has the attribute pbn_fake = TRUE.

read_blocks()

read_blocks() returns <version>_results/real/blocks.qs2 when it exists. Else it returns the blocks.qs2 of the scenario real of this computer, and it gives a warning that the numbers are fake. In a one-file project that file is <version>_results/fake/blocks.qs2. In a project that is not one-file it is real/blocks.qs2 itself, so read_blocks() stops. txt() and make_checklists() read the blocks in the same way. The rule built_reads_source of check_project() says which functions a manuscript in manuscript/built/ MUST use.

The values are fake when they come from another file than real/blocks.qs2, or when real/blocks.qs2 has pbn_fake = TRUE. For fake values in a document that knitr renders, such as a .qmd or an .Rmd, read_blocks(), txt() and make_checklists() add a knitr document hook. The hook puts the line **FAKE DATA** once at the top of the output, after the YAML header. A document that reads only real values gets no such line.

See also

vignette("pbn"), section "Running on an air-gapped server".
